mainTopic: The order and manner of the יום כיפור blood service on the golden altar: where the כהן stands, which corner he starts at, and why (רבי עקיבא vs. רבי יוסי הגלילי).
overview: The משנה identifies the altar 'before ה׳' as the golden altar. It describes how the כהן גדול put the יום כיפור blood on its four corners, starting at the northeast, while רבי אליעזר says he stood in one place. It then describes the seven sprinklings on the altar's top, where the leftover blood was poured, and how the blood was sold to gardeners and carries מעילה. The גמרא brings two ברייתות of רבי נחמיה. On יום הכפורים the כהן stands on the inner side of the altar ('ויצא'). For the פר העלם דבר של צבור he stands on its outer side ('מזבח לפני ה׳ ואין כהן לפני ה׳'). Next comes a מחלוקת: רבי עקיבא starts at the southeast corner, and רבי יוסי הגלילי starts at the northeast. Both agree he skips the first corner he reaches, because of שמואל's reading of 'ויצא אל המזבח'. The גמרא first suggests they argue about רמי בר יחזקאל's rule to always turn right, but rejects this. The real argument is whether the inner service is learned from the outer one. רבי עקיבא's order is finally explained by 'ויצא אל המזבח' combined with ריש לקיש's rule אין מעבירין על המצות.

steps.title: Identifying the altar 'before ה׳' as the golden altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes the פסוק and says the altar 'before ה׳' is the inner golden altar (מזבח הזהב).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: 'And he shall go out to the altar that is before ה׳.' This is the golden altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה quotes a פסוק from the יום כיפור service and tells us which altar it means: the golden altar inside the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two altars: the outer copper altar in the courtyard and the inner golden altar in the היכל. The words 'before ה׳' point to the inner one, which stands closest to the קודש הקדשים. Everything that follows in the משנה is about blood placed on this golden altar.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall go out', from the פסוק in ויקרא ט״ז
'Before ה׳', meaning inside, near the Holy of Holies
The golden (inner) altar, used for incense

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two altars. In this משנה, 'the altar' means the inner golden altar unless the text explicitly says 'מזבח החיצון' (the outer altar).

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
'And he shall go out to the altar that is before the Lord'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ויקרא ט״ז:י״ח.

phrases.english: this is the golden altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיָצָא אֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֲשֶׁר לִפְנֵי ה׳ זֶה מִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The altar 'before ה׳' in ויקרא ט״ז:י״ח is the inner golden altar.

steps.title: The order of corners on the golden altar
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול starts at the northeast corner and goes around to northwest, southwest, and finally southeast. That last corner is where the outer altar's חטאת service begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: He began cleansing the altar, going along. Where does he begin? From the northeast corner, then northwest, then southwest, then southeast. The place where he begins a חטאת on the outer altar is where he finishes on the inner altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists, corner by corner, the order in which the כהן גדול puts blood on the four corners of the golden altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is northeast, northwest, southwest, southeast. The משנה gives a memory tool: the southeast corner, where a regular חטאת on the outer altar starts, is where the inner altar finishes.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleansing or purifying (the altar) with blood
The outer (copper) altar in the courtyard

steps.whyThisMatters: The link to the outer altar gives a fixed reference point, the southeast corner, which makes the order easy to remember.

phrases.english: He began to cleanse (the altar) and proceed,
phrases.notes: Some read this as sprinkling while moving downward.

phrases.english: From where does he begin?
From the northeast corner,
(then) northwest,
(then) southwest, (then) southeast.
The place where he begins with a sin-offering
on the outer altar,

phrases.aramaic: מִשָּׁם הָיָה גּוֹמֵר עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי.
phrases.english: from there he would finish on the inner altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the altar has been identified, the משנה describes the order of the service on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order of corners: NE, NW, SW, SE. He finishes at the corner where the outer altar's חטאת begins.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: he stood in one place
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that the כהן גדול did not walk around the altar. He stood in one spot and put blood on all four corners from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: He would stand in his place and cleanse (all the corners).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a different picture: the כהן גדול stayed in one spot and did not walk around the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view in the משנה has him walking from corner to corner. רבי אליעזר says he stood still and reached every corner, which works because the golden altar was small (one אמה by one אמה). The order of corners is not the issue here. The argument is about whether he moves.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues with the first opinion
In his place, without moving around

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
He would stand in his place and cleanse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A competing view about how the כהן גדול reached the corners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול stands in one place and does not walk around the altar.

steps.title: Placing the blood upward on all corners except the one in front
steps.stepSummary: On every corner he placed the blood with an upward motion, except the corner directly in front of him, where he placed it with a downward motion.
steps.simpleTranslation: On all of them he would place (the blood) from below upward, except for the one in front of him, on which he would place it from above downward.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the hand motion used on each corner. Most corners get an upward motion, and one corner gets a downward motion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on where the כהן is standing. For the corner right in front of him, a downward stroke is natural. For the others, he brings his hand from below upward. This detail fits naturally with רבי אליעזר's picture of the כהן standing in one place.

phrases.english: And on all of them he would place (the blood)
from below upward,
except for the one that was in front of him,
on which he would place it from above downward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל כּוּלָּן הָיָה נוֹתֵן מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which corners to how the blood is placed on them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Upward motion on every corner except the one directly in front, which gets a downward motion.

steps.title: Seven sprinklings on the top, and the leftover blood poured at the western base
steps.stepSummary: He sprinkled seven times on the top of the golden altar, then poured the leftover blood at the western base of the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sprinkled on the pure (top) of the altar seven times, and the remainder of the blood he would pour onto the western base of the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: After the corners, the כהן גדול sprinkles seven times on the top surface of the golden altar. He then brings the leftover blood outside and pours it at the base of the outer altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate acts are listed here: placing blood on the corners (earlier) and sprinkling seven times on the altar's top surface (טהרו). The leftover blood (שירי הדם) is not simply thrown away. It goes to the western side of the outer altar's base, the side facing the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'pure' surface of the altar, its top, cleared down to the gold
The leftover blood after the required placements
The base (foundation) of the outer altar

phrases.english: He sprinkled on the pure (top) of the altar
seven times,
and the remainder of the blood he would pour
onto the western base
of the outer altar,

steps.triggerLanguage: הִזָּה עַל טׇהֳרוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the service after the corners: the seven sprinklings and the leftover blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven sprinklings on the top of the golden altar. The leftover blood goes to the western base of the outer altar.

steps.title: Leftover blood of outer-altar offerings goes to the southern base
steps.stepSummary: As a side note, the leftover blood from offerings done on the outer altar was poured at its southern base.
steps.simpleTranslation: And (the leftover blood) of the outer altar he would pour onto the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a related rule: blood left over from offerings done on the outer altar itself goes to a different side of the base, the southern side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a contrast. Blood from the inner service goes to the western base, the side facing the היכל. Blood from the outer altar's own offerings goes to the southern base. This prepares the next line, which talks about both kinds of blood together (אלו ואלו).

keyTerms.meaning: The southern base of the outer altar

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about the יום כיפור inner blood anymore. It is about leftover blood from offerings done on the outer altar.

phrases.english: And (the leftover blood) of the outer altar
he would pour onto the southern base.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ אֶל יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related contrast to the western-base rule just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover blood of outer-altar offerings is poured at the southern base.

steps.title: The blood flows to נחל קדרון, is sold to gardeners, and carries מעילה
steps.stepSummary: Both kinds of leftover blood mix in the channel, flow out to נחל קדרון, and are sold to gardeners as fertilizer. Using them without paying counts as מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These and those mix in the channel and flow out to נחל קדרון. They are sold to gardeners for fertilizer, and one who uses them without paying commits מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה follows the blood after the service is over. It drains out of the מקדש and is sold, and it stays holy until it is paid for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even blood that has finished its job on the altar is still הקדש. That is why gardeners must buy it; using it for free would be מעילה (misusing holy property). The phrase אלו ואלו ties together the two kinds of blood from steps 5 and 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a water channel (not the measurement 'cubit')
The Kidron stream outside the מקדש
One is liable for מעילה, the misuse of holy property

steps.whatToRemember: Summary of the משנה: altar = golden altar. Corners NE, NW, SW, SE (רבי אליעזר: he stands in one place). Upward motion except the corner in front. Seven sprinklings on top. Leftover blood to the western base (outer-altar blood to the southern base). All of it flows to קדרון, is sold, and carries מעילה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here אמה means a water channel, not the measurement 'cubit'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that קדושה stays attached to sacrificial blood even after the service, until it is redeemed by sale.

phrases.english: These and those mix together in the channel
and flow out to the Kidron stream,
and are sold to gardeners for fertilizer,
and one is liable for misuse (of sacred property) with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two kinds of leftover blood and states what finally happens to them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover blood is sold to gardeners and remains subject to מעילה until it is bought.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'and he shall go out to the altar'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what the words ״ויצא אל המזבח״ come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: 'And he shall go out to the altar.' What does the פסוק come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that asks why the תורה needed to write 'and he shall go out to the altar.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: After sprinkling toward the curtain, the כהן גדול reaches the golden altar anyway, so the words 'he shall go out' look unnecessary. The question 'מה תלמוד לומר' assumes every extra word in the תורה teaches something. This sets up the answer that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does the פסוק come to teach?'; asks why a phrase is needed

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught:
'And he shall go out to the altar.'
What does the verse come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוק quoted at the opening of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra halacha is learned from the apparently unnecessary words 'and he shall go out to the altar'?

steps.title: רבי נחמיה begins: a comparison to the פר העלם דבר
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה starts his answer. With the communal-error bull, the כהן stands past the altar when sprinkling toward the curtain, so one might think the same is true here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: Because we find with the bull brought for (an error in) any of the מצוות that the כהן stands beyond the altar and sprinkles toward the curtain when he sprinkles, one might think that here too it is so...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה begins to answer the question. First he sets up a mistaken assumption (a הוה אמינא) that the פסוק will need to correct, and his answer continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the פר העלם דבר של ציבור, the כהן stands on the outer (eastern) side of the golden altar, so the altar is between him and the curtain, and he sprinkles toward the curtain. Someone might assume the יום כיפור sprinkling works the same way. The words 'יכול אף זה כן' signal that the פסוק ״ויצא אל המזבח״ is about to show that יום כיפור is different.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who answers the ברייתא's question
The bull brought for a communal error in any מצוה‎ (פר העלם דבר של ציבור)
The curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים
'One might think this case is the same'; introduces a הוה אמינא that will be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: It continues in the next step. 'יכול אף זה כן' is only the mistaken assumption, not his conclusion. The פסוק's correction comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said:
Because we find
with the bull brought for (an error in) any of the commandments,
that the priest stands beyond the altar
and sprinkles toward the curtain
at the time that he sprinkles,
one might think that this, too, is the same,

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּפַר הַבָּא עַל כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the מה תלמוד לומר question by setting up a הוה אמינא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial so far: the פסוק is needed to stop us from copying the פר העלם דבר's standing position. The full answer continues next.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the כהן stands beyond the altar with the פר העלם דבר, one might think the כהן גדול does the same on יום כיפור.

steps.title: On יום הכפורים the כהן stood on the inner side of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה finishes his answer. The words 'ויצא אל המזבח' show that on יום הכפורים the כהן was on the inner side of the altar before he went out to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: 'And he shall go out to the altar.' Where was he before that? On the inner side of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה finishes his answer. The verse says the כהן 'goes out' to the altar, so he must have been standing on its inner side while sprinkling toward the curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, someone might have thought יום הכפורים works like פר העלם דבר של צבור, where the כהן stands outside the altar. The word 'ויצא' (he goes out) only makes sense if he was further in, between the golden altar and the curtain. So on יום הכפורים the כהן stands לפנים מן המזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: On the inner (western) side of the altar, closer to the curtain

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'And he shall go out to the altar.'
Where was he? On the inner side of the altar.
phrases.notes: Inner side means between the golden altar and the curtain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי נחמיה's answer, which step 9 began.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ויצא' teaches that on יום הכפורים the כהן stood on the inner side of the altar.

steps.title: A second ברייתא asks why the verse says 'before ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא asks what the words 'לפני ה׳' come to teach in the passage about פר העלם דבר של צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: 'Before ה׳.' What does the verse come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that asks why the verse about פר העלם דבר של צבור says 'לפני ה׳'. This sets up רבי נחמיה's answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the first ברייתא. That one asked about יום הכפורים, and this one asks about the communal-error bull. The question assumes the words 'לפני ה׳' must teach us something.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought for a communal error

phrases.english: It was taught in another ברייתא:
'Before ה׳': what does the verse come to teach?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: ״לִפְנֵי ה׳״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel ברייתא about פר העלם דבר של צבור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'לפני ה׳' teach about the communal-error bull.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: one might think it works like יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה explains the first idea one might have had. On יום הכפורים the כהן stands on the inner side of the altar, so maybe he does the same for the communal-error bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: We find with the bull and goat of יום הכפורים that the כהן stands on the inner side of the altar and sprinkles toward the curtain. So one might think this case is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה begins his answer by laying out a mistaken idea. The next step will correct it with a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since step 10 showed the כהן stands inside the altar on יום הכפורים, one might copy that rule to the communal-error bull. Both sprinklings go toward the curtain, so the comparison seems natural. This is only the הוה אמינא, the first guess, which the verse will reject.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים
One might think this case is the same

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said:
Since we find with the bull and the goat
of Yom Kippur
that the Kohen stands on the inner side of the altar
and sprinkles toward the curtain
when he sprinkles,
one might think this one too is the same,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 11's question by stating the mistaken first guess.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial answer: it sets up the guess that the communal-error bull follows the יום הכפורים position.

steps.title: The altar is before ה׳, but the כהן stands outside it
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'מזבח קטרת הסמים לפני ה׳'. So only the altar is 'before ה׳', and for the communal-error bull the כהן stands on the outer side of the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: 'The altar of sweet incense before ה׳, which is in the Tent of Meeting.' The altar is before ה׳, but the כהן is not. How so? He stands outside the altar and sprinkles.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה brings a verse that rejects the first guess. For the communal-error bull, the כהן stands on the outer side of the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls the altar, not the כהן, 'לפני ה׳'. So nothing of the כהן should be further in than the altar, and he stands on its eastern side. The two cases now have opposite rules: on יום הכפורים he stands inside, and for פר העלם דבר של צבור he stands outside.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar of sweet incense, which is the golden altar
On the outer (eastern) side of the altar

steps.whatToRemember: On יום הכפורים the כהן stands on the inner side of the golden altar ('ויצא'). For פר העלם דבר של צבור he stands on its outer side ('מזבח לפני ה׳ ואין כהן לפני ה׳').
steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות are not arguing with each other. Each one teaches the rule for a different offering, and the rules are opposite.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'The altar of sweet incense before ה׳'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ויקרא ד:ז.

phrases.english: 'which is in the Tent of Meeting'
the altar is before ה׳,
but the Kohen is not before ה׳.
How so?
He stands outside the altar and sprinkles.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִזְבַּח קְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֲשֶׁר בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the guess of step 12 using a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the communal-error bull, the כהן stands on the outer side of the altar.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן stands inside the altar, as on יום הכפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the altar is 'לפני ה׳', so the כהן stands outside it.

steps.title: Which corner did he start cleansing the altar from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'התחיל מחטא ויורד' and brings a ברייתא that asks which corner the כהן began from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He began to cleanse, going downward,' and so on. The Rabbis taught: 'He began to cleanse, going downward.' From where would he begin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and opens a new topic: the order of the corners on the golden altar. This question sets up a מחלוקת in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says he put blood on the corners but does not say where he started. The ברייתא fills in that missing detail.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleansing (putting blood on the altar to purify it)
The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] 'He began to cleanse, going downward,' etc.
The Rabbis taught:
He began to cleanse, going downward.
From where would he begin?

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְחִיל מְחַטֵּא וְיוֹרֵד וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and starts a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting corner and the order of the corners.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: start at the southeast corner
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the כהן starts at the southeast corner. He then goes to the southwest, the northwest, and finally the northeast corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the southeast corner, then southwest, then northwest, then northeast. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the question: start at the southeast corner and go around through the south first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His route goes southeast, southwest, northwest, northeast. The north-eastern corner is last.

phrases.english: From the southeast corner,
[then] southwest,
[then] northwest,
[then] northeast,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Start at the southeast corner, then southwest, northwest, northeast.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: start at the northeast corner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees. The כהן starts at the northeast corner, then goes to the northwest, the southwest, and ends at the southeast corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: From the northeast corner, then northwest, then southwest, then southeast.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי gives a different order. He starts in the north and finishes at the corner where רבי עקיבא began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both views the כהן goes around all four corners. They disagree about the starting corner, and so about which way he goes around. The גמרא will next look into the reasoning behind each view.

keyTerms.meaning: An early תנא who argues with רבי עקיבא here

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת about the order of the corners sets up the גמרא's next discussion of why each תנא picks his starting point.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
From the northeast corner,
[then] northwest,
[then] southwest,
[then] southeast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a view that disagrees with רבי עקיבא in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Start at the northeast corner, then northwest, southwest, and southeast.

steps.title: The two opinions are mirror images
steps.stepSummary: The starting corner of one opinion is the ending corner of the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The place where רבי יוסי הגלילי starts is where רבי עקיבא stops. The place where רבי עקיבא starts is where רבי יוסי הגלילי stops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a neat pattern in the two opinions we just saw. Each one starts where the other one ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי starts at the northeast corner, and that is where רבי עקיבא finishes. רבי עקיבא starts at the southeast corner, and that is where רבי יוסי הגלילי finishes. So they walk the same path around the altar, but in opposite directions.
steps.whyThisMatters: Seeing that the paths are opposite sets up the coming question: which direction is the 'correct' way to turn?

phrases.english: The place where Rabbi Yosei HaGelili begins,
there Rabbi Akiva ends.
The place where Rabbi Akiva begins,
there Rabbi Yosei HaGelili ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מַתְחִיל, שָׁם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא פּוֹסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the two opinions from steps 15 and 16 and shows they are reverse paths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two opinions follow the same route in opposite directions.

steps.title: Both agree he skips the first corner he reaches
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees the כהן does not begin at the first corner he comes to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees, at least, that he does not do the sprinkling at the corner he reaches first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out one thing both opinions agree on. The כהן does not start at the first corner he walks up to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן comes out of the inner area from the west, so the first corners he meets are on the western side of the altar. Yet both רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי have him start at an eastern corner. So both agree he walks past the first corner without using it.

phrases.english: According to everyone, in any case,
at that corner which he encounters first —
phrases.notes: A western corner, since he comes from the west

phrases.english: he does not perform the sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing how the opinions differ, the גמרא notes a point they share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one begins at the first corner the כהן reaches.

steps.title: Why skip the first corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason he does not begin at the first corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the כהן walks past the first corner. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you would expect someone to start at the nearest corner. Since both opinions skip it, there must be a source, and the גמרא wants to know it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the agreed rule in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for skipping the first corner.

steps.title: שמואל: he must go out past the whole altar
steps.stepSummary: שמואל learns from 'ויצא אל המזבח' that the כהן must first go past the entire altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Because the verse says, 'And he shall go out to the altar,' meaning he does not start until he has gone out past the whole altar.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question with a verse. The word 'ויצא' (go out) teaches that the כהן must first walk past the entire altar before starting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coming from the west, the כהן reaches the western corners first, but he is still 'inside' and has not yet 'gone out' past the altar. Only when he reaches the eastern side has he 'gone out', so he starts at an eastern corner.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the source here
'And he shall go out to the altar' (ויקרא טז:יח)

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Because the verse says:
"And he shall go out to the altar,"
meaning, until he goes out past the entire altar.
phrases.notes: He reaches the eastern side before he begins

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'ויצא אל המזבח' requires him to pass the whole altar first, so he starts on the east side.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי עקיבא have him turn right?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: the כהן should go around to the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, let him go around to the right!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי עקיבא's direction. It argues the כהן should circle to the right, not the left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן stands on the east side facing west, so his right hand is toward the north. Turning right means going to the northeast corner first, as רבי יוסי הגלילי says. רבי עקיבא has him start at the southeast and move toward his left, which seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of the right / turning rightward

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva,
let him go around by way of the right!
phrases.notes: Facing west, his right is toward the north

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the starting side is clear, the גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's route (southeast, then southwest, and so on).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In Temple service, turns should be to the right, but רבי עקיבא's route turns to the left.

steps.title: Suggestion: they argue about רמי בר יחזקאל's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two תנאים disagree about the rule of רמי בר יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they disagree about the teaching of רמי בר יחזקאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation. Maybe רבי עקיבא simply does not accept the rule that one must turn right. The next step quotes that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying רבי עקיבא made a mistake, the גמרא suggests the argument is about a basic principle. The word 'לימא' marks this as only a suggestion, not a final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who taught the rule of turning right

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' is only a suggestion. The גמרא is testing an idea, not deciding the matter.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא בִּדְרָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל קָא מִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about the teaching of Rami bar Yeḥezkel?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְרָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge of step 21 by framing it as a dispute over a principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the dispute as a disagreement over a principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's leftward route seems to break the rule of turning right.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי עקיבא does not hold of that rule at all.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל learns 'turn right' from שלמה's Sea
steps.stepSummary: From the order of the oxen under the Sea that שלמה built, רמי בר יחזקאל learns that all turns should be to the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל said: About the Sea that שלמה made, the verse says, 'It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east, and the Sea was on top of them, and their back ends were all toward the inside.' So you learn that every turn you make should only be to the right, toward the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching and its source. He learns from the order of the oxen in the verse that turns should go to the right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse lists the groups of oxen in a set order: north, west, south, east. רמי בר יחזקאל reads this order as a model for turning: always rightward, moving toward the east. This is the principle the גמרא thinks רבי יוסי הגלילי follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The large water basin ('the Sea') that שלמה built
Twelve oxen that held up the Sea

phrases.english: As Rami bar Yeḥezkel said:
The Sea that Solomon made —
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from דברי הימים ב ד:ד.

phrases.english: "It stood upon twelve oxen,
three facing north,
and three facing west,
and three facing south,
and three facing east,
and the Sea was set upon them above,
and all their back ends were inward."
So you have learned
that all the turns that you make

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין, לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: should only be by way of the right, toward the east.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching mentioned in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that all turns in the service should be to the right.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the oxen under שלמה's Sea in דברי הימים ב ד:ד.

steps.title: One holds of רמי בר יחזקאל, the other does not
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is spelled out: רבי יוסי הגלילי follows רמי בר יחזקאל, and רבי עקיבא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This master holds of רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching, and this master does not hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion. רבי יוסי הגלילי accepts the 'turn right' rule, and רבי עקיבא does not, which is why his route goes the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the challenge from step 21. רבי עקיבא is not ignoring a rule he accepts; he simply does not accept it. Since this was introduced with 'לימא', it is only a proposal, and the next step rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: And this master does not hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions start on the east side because of 'ויצא אל המזבח'. The גמרא first suggests they differ over רמי בר יחזקאל's 'always turn right' rule. The very next step rejects this suggestion.

phrases.aramaic: מָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל,
phrases.english: This master holds of the teaching of Rami bar Yeḥezkel,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל.
phrases.english: and this master does not hold of the teaching of Rami bar Yeḥezkel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל, וּמָר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רמי בר יחזקאל's rule from step 23 to the two תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא should require turning right.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא does not accept רמי בר יחזקאל's rule, so he has no need to turn right.

steps.title: Both sides accept רמי בר יחזקאל; the real argument is about learning inside from outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that רבי עקיבא disagrees with רמי בר יחזקאל. Everyone agrees with him. The real argument is whether the inner altar's service is learned from the outer altar's service.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds like רמי בר יחזקאל. Here is what they argue about: one תנא holds that we learn the inside service from the outside service, and the other holds that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'no' to its own earlier suggestion. It gives a new reason why the two תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said רבי עקיבא rejects the rule that every turn goes to the right. Now the גמרא says both agree with that rule. The real argument is whether that rule, which governs the outer altar, carries over to the inner altar. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it does, so the כהן turns right on the inner altar too. רבי עקיבא says it does not, so the 'turn right' rule never gets applied to the inner altar in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: No, everyone agrees. This is a formula that rejects a suggested argument.
Inside: the service on the inner (golden) altar in the היכל
Outside: the service on the outer altar in the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not rejecting רמי בר יחזקאל's rule. He agrees with it. He just holds that the outside pattern does not carry over to the inside altar.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole debate. It is no longer about a rule of direction. It is about whether one עבודה can serve as a model for another.

phrases.english: No, everyone
holds like Rami bar Yeḥezkel.
phrases.notes: His teaching is that all turns should be to the right.

phrases.english: And here they disagree about this:
One Sage holds: we derive inside from outside,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָא יָלְפִינַן פְּנִים מִחוּץ.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: we do not derive inside from outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation given in step 24 and replaces it with a new explanation of the argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that the argument depends on רמי בר יחזקאל. The argument itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion wrongly assumed that רבי עקיבא rejects the 'turn right' rule. In fact the argument is about learning פנים from חוץ.

steps.title: Without an outside model, why does רבי עקיבא require a set order?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא does not learn the inside service from the outside service, it seems there should be no required order at all. The כהן should be able to start wherever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let's grant that רבי עקיבא does not learn inside from outside. Then if he wants he should do it this way, and if he wants he should do it that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא. Without the outside model, where does his fixed order come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking away the outside model also takes away the reason for any particular starting point. So רבי עקיבא's fixed order now seems to have no source. The challenge demands a reason that does not come from the outer altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that... This opens a 'let's grant this, but still' challenge.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, granted
that he does not derive inside from outside,
if he wants, let him do it this way,
if he wants, let him do it that way?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נְהִי דְּלָא יָלֵיף פְּנִים מִחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new explanation from step 25 by asking where רבי עקיבא's fixed order comes from.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's fixed starting corner on the inner altar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the outside model is removed, there is no source for any required order, so the order should be the כהן's free choice.

steps.title: By right, he should start at the corner he reaches first
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that there is a basic rule even without the outside model. The כהן should start at the first corner he comes to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא would tell you: by right, at the corner he meets first, there he should do the sprinkling first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. His order comes from a separate rule: start with whatever corner you reach first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is not free choice. It is decided by which corner the כהן reaches first on his way. That rule stands on its own and does not need the outer altar as a model.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you. The גמרא answers on behalf of an earlier authority.
By the strict rule; by right

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva would say to you:
By right, at that corner
that he reaches first,
at that one he should perform first,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supplies a separate source for the order that does not depend on the outer altar.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the outside model, the כהן may start at any corner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order follows the corner he reaches first.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: do not pass over a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The rule 'start at the first corner' comes from ריש לקיש's principle אין מעבירין על המצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: we do not pass over מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the 'first corner' rule from step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a chance to do a מצוה is right in front of you, you may not skip it to do another one later. So the corner the כהן meets first is the corner he must do first.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not pass over מצוות. Do the מצוה in front of you first.

steps.whyThisMatters: אין מעבירין על המצות is a well-known principle used all over ש״ס, for example with תפילין and טלית.

phrases.english: as Reish Lakish said:
One does not pass over commandments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule stated in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן must start at the corner he reaches first
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's rule אין מעבירין על המצות

steps.title: So why doesn't he start at that first corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, in practice, the כהן does not start at the corner he reaches first, which is on the western side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why doesn't he do so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question. If the rule is 'first corner first,' why doesn't the actual order start there? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן has just sprinkled toward the פרוכת, standing on the inner (western) side of the golden altar, so he reaches the altar's western corners first. Yet רבי עקיבא's order does not begin there. The question asks for the reason.

phrases.english: And why does he not do so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out a gap between the rule in steps 27 and 28 and the actual order of sprinkling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the כהן does not begin at the corner he reaches first

steps.title: 'ויצא אל המזבח' means he first goes past the whole altar
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ויצא אל המזבח requires the כהן to go out past the entire altar before he begins. So the western corners are not where he can start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written, 'And he shall go out to the altar': he does not begin until he has gone out past the whole altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A פסוק forces the כהן to walk past the whole altar first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reuses שמואל's reading from step 20. Because of this פסוק, the כהן cannot start on the western side, even though he passes it first. He begins on the eastern side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall go out to the altar' (ויקרא טז:יח)

phrases.english: Because it is written: 'And he shall go out to the altar,'
until he goes out past the entire altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires him to pass the entire altar first, so he cannot begin at the western corner.

steps.title: After the first eastern corner, he returns to the corner he skipped
steps.stepSummary: Once he has sprinkled on the eastern corner, he goes back to the western corner he had to skip. That corner was really the one he should have done first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once he has given the blood on that corner, he comes back to the corner where he really should have given it first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי עקיבא's order. It combines the two rules: the פסוק and אין מעבירין על המצות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק pushes the first sprinkling to the eastern side. After that, אין מעבירין על המצות sends him straight back to the western corner he passed over. That is why רבי עקיבא's order does not simply go to the right all the way around.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's order comes from two rules working together. The פסוק ויצא אל המזבח makes him start past the whole altar. Then אין מעבירין על המצות sends him back to the corner he first passed. It does not come from copying the outer altar.

phrases.english: And once he has given the blood on that corner,
he comes back to that corner
where he was obligated to give first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings together step 30's פסוק with steps 27 and 28's rule to explain the full order.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's fixed order comes from ויצא אל המזבח together with אין מעבירין על המצות, without learning פנים from חוץ.
